answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring each identity to a costly, slowly grown reputation orchard: an agent must first complete real tasks attested by independent peers before it earns anything. New identities start with zero trust and must bridge upward from low-value work, so spinning up thousands of fakes costs real compute and time per identity while the payoff per identity stays low, because trust, not headcount, gates rewards. Reputation cannot be copied or transferred, so the marginal cost of each fake identity exceeds its expected gain.
